# Hard stops (HS-v1)

These apply to every session, every role, every card. If a step would cross
one, stop the step, write what was needed in your return file with status
`BLOCKED`, and do nothing else for that step.

- **HS-1 Live data.** Never open, list, read, copy, back up, restore or
  query the live Apunta data folder, its backups, the owner's Claude export
  or Halaxy PDFs. Never contact port **7717**. Never run
  `scripts/recover-current-linux.mjs` or `scripts/smoke-live.mjs`.
- **HS-2 Isolation.** Every command that starts an Apunta server, opens a
  database or launches the app runs through `scripts/v2/sandbox.mjs` once
  card P0.3 is APPROVED. Before that, only non-launching edits and unit
  tests that use in-memory or temporary databases created by the test.
- **HS-3 Downloads.** Only items in `docs/v2/ACQUISITION.md`, by the rules
  there. Never pull an Ollama tag that already exists locally. Never
  remove or replace an Ollama model.
- **HS-4 Git.** Work only on `feature/v2`, starting from the base commit the
  coordinator gave you. Never merge into `main`, pull, rebase, reset,
  force-push, rewrite history, or change repository visibility. Stage
  explicit paths only.
- **HS-5 Secrets.** Never create, print, copy or commit a production
  signing key or password. Test keys live only inside a sandbox run folder.
- **HS-6 Network at runtime.** No new network access from `server/`, `web/`
  or `shared/`. The only runtime exceptions are model acquisition (existing)
  and the update check in the Tauri shell (contract C-UPD).
- **HS-7 Safety instruments.** Never loosen a scorer, guard, lock, test or
  threshold to make a result pass. Never change a threshold in
  `docs/v2/CONTRACTS.md`.
- **HS-8 Fabricated data only.** Fixtures, audio, screenshots and examples
  are fabricated. English uses the prototype's sample people; Spanish uses
  only names in `e2e/fixtures/eval-es/NAMES.md`.
- **HS-9 Protected paths.** Never edit `prototype/`. Never edit files outside
  your card's "May edit" list.
- **HS-10 Owner-only actions.** Never enable Spanish in release builds, write
  the owner's clinical verdict, publish a release, create GitHub secrets, or
  stop or inspect the live v1 instance.

## Fixed decisions
1. **What becomes a key.** Visible text, aria labels, titles, placeholders,
   empty states, toasts and errors are all catalogue keys, and "Apunta" is
   never translated. This holds for a string **wherever** it is written: a JSX
   text node, one of the four visible attributes, a module-level const, or the
   argument of a thrown `Error`. Such a string is a **UI** key, not
   `errors.<code>`: S2.2's Fixed decision 9 reserves that namespace for the
   server's codes and S2.5 owns the list. This card owns far more of the hard
   class than S2.3 did, so the rule is restated rather than inherited: a
   module const that reaches the screen is a key, exactly as S2.3 made
   `RefineColumn.tsx:15` one.
2. **Keep-as-is tokens, and the only legitimate way to add one.** A keep-as-is
   token that is a **whole literal** (`BrandMark`'s and `BrandWordmark`'s
   `aria-label="Apunta"`, and nothing else in the owned set today) stays in
   `scripts/check-ui-strings.allow.json`, matched whole — a token may be added
   **only** when the whole literal it matches is a product name, an identifier
   or a file name, which is the shape of the ten seeded tokens
   (`check-ui-strings.mjs:44-47`). Adding one to make a row green is HS-7, and
   the response is a `BLOCKED` return naming the `file:line`. A keep-as-is
   token **inside** a translatable sentence is the opposite case: it is
   preserved verbatim in **both** catalogue values, never allowlisted, never
   dropped, never translated, and never split off into a key of its own —
   because the allowlist matches whole strings only (`:248`). The known case is
   `Capture.tsx:389`, `{formatTimer(seconds)} recorded. Nothing has left this
   Mac.`: one key for the whole sentence, with `Mac` verbatim in both values,
   even though `Mac` is already in the allowlist as a whole-literal token.
   That pairing is the trap — a file this card may edit, and a matching entry
   already in the list. `PlanGoalCard.tsx:43`'s `const BLANK = '—'` is the
   other known shape: a separator, which renders as it is in any language and
   is not a key at all.
3. **A date reaches a catalogue as a parameter, never as English text.**
   `PrepView.tsx:174` composes `Review due {formatPlanDate(…)}.`, and
   `formatPlanDate` returns English (`format.ts:90-95`, the hardcoded `en-US`
   `Intl.DateTimeFormat` of `:20-24`). It becomes one key whose parameter is
   declared **`dateOnly`**, because `review_due` is a calendar date
   (`YYYY-MM-DD`) and a `date` (instant) parameter would shift the day west of
   Greenwich. `BackupCard.tsx:393` composes **no English date at all** —
   `instantToLocalDay` already returns a raw `YYYY-MM-DD` — so it is a stored
   value under Fixed decision 4 (a raw parameter), not a `date`; changing it to
   `date` would alter visible English and break `BackupCard.test.tsx:170`.
   **Passing the pre-formatted English as a parameter is the failure this
   decision forbids**: V1 goes green, English is unchanged, and the briefing
   keeps saying `Aug 8, 2026` in Spanish until S2.7's copy review finds it. No
   line of `format.ts` or `plural.ts` changes — they stay the oracle.
4. **Stored values are parameters, never keys.** `PlanView.tsx:192` and `:289`
   render `Version {current.version} · {current.status}`: `version` and
   `status` are stored values and go into the catalogue as parameters of one
   key, verbatim, in both languages. C-LANG@1 rule 5 is the reason — guards use
   section roles, not strings, and stored strings are not rewritten. A status
   that needs a display name is a key with the stored value as its parameter,
   not a translation of the stored value.
5. **The checker is necessary, not sufficient, and the two blind spots are
   pinned by tests.** A literal is "JSX text nodes plus the `placeholder`,
   `aria-label`, `title` and `alt` string attributes" (`:29-36`), and the
   pieces JSX leaves when it splits a sentence around an interpolation are
   deliberately unreported. So V1 at `TOTAL 0` is compatible with in-scope
   strings still hardcoded, and this card has more of them than S2.3 did:
   `BackupCard.tsx:180,315-318,393`, `PrepView.tsx:174`,
   `NotesColumn.tsx:132`, `PlanView.tsx:304`, `InstructionsPanel.tsx:124`,
   `BrainstormView.tsx:176-178`. Each
   is one key with the interpolated value as a parameter — never two keys
   either side of the interpolation. Each is pinned where a row can see it: the
   owned test files gain cases asserting the rendered text is the catalogue's
   English, in `BackupCard.test.tsx` and `PrepView.test.tsx` for the two date
   sentences and `BrainstormView.test.tsx` for its empty state. Both files
   exist and V2 collects them.
6. **The catalogue grows; the guard does not.** New keys go into both
   `en.ts` and `es-MX.ts` and nowhere else, and the type-level parity rule
   (S2.2's Fixed decision 2) is what stops a key `es-MX` lacks — V4 is its
   only witness, since vitest strips types. A key this card cannot fill with a
   real es-MX string is **reported, not filled with the English**: this is the
   card that adds the large majority of the keys, and an English string in
   `es-MX.ts` passes every row here and is first caught by S2.7's copy review,
   three steps downstream.
7. **English is unchanged.** Every English value this card writes is the
   English the app produces today, character for character (S2.2's Fixed
   decision 6, C-LANG@1 rules 3 and 5). A key whose English is not what the
   screen shows today is a stop, not a copy improvement — S2.7 and S2.8 own the
   copy.
8. **The switch is one line, and only one.** `REPORT_ONLY` at `:62` goes from
   `true` to `false`, and nothing else in `scripts/check-ui-strings.mjs` moves.
   Stated because V1's criterion (`TOTAL 0`) is reachable three ways — by
   extracting the strings, by emptying `DEFAULT_ROOTS` (`:68`) or
   `SCANNED_EXTENSIONS` (`:71`), or by inverting the `allowlist.has` filter
   (`:248`) — and the second set makes every row green with the guard scanning
   nothing. The second set is out of May edit above, and V5 is the row that
   witnesses the difference.

## Stop conditions
- A literal in a file this card does not own — `web/src/lib/`,
  `web/src/hooks/`, `web/src/api/`, or any of S2.3's fourteen components — is
  a `BLOCKED` return naming its `file:line`. May edit is not widened and
  `scripts/check-ui-strings.allow.json` is **not** edited to absorb it (HS-7,
  HS-9). The known pair is `web/src/lib/recorder.ts:48-56` and
  `web/src/hooks/useDictation.ts:8-9,85`, dispositioned above: they stay
  English and are reported as a finding for a later card.
- A literal in `web/src/App.tsx` that `useI18n()` cannot reach, because it
  renders **above** `I18nProvider` (`:41-52`): a `BLOCKED` return naming the
  line and saying why. The mount does not move — it reads `language` through
  `SettingsProvider` (`i18n.tsx:82-88`) — so do not add a second provider and
  do not allowlist the string.
- A string built by concatenation that cannot be one key with parameters:
  **report** it with its location, and do not split it into two keys to make
  it fit. `PlanView.tsx:192,289` is the known shape and its answer is one key
  with two parameters, `BackupCard.tsx:315-318` one key with four.
- A literal that can be neither keyed nor allowlisted — `Capture.tsx:389`'s
  `Mac` inside its sentence is the known in-sentence case, and
  `PlanGoalCard.tsx:43`'s `'—'` the known separator — is **reported** with its
  `file:line`; the allowlist is not edited to absorb it, the sentence is not
  split, and the separator is not turned into a key (HS-7, HS-9). The response
  is a `BLOCKED` return naming the line, not a new key invented to dodge the
  question.
- The bare default would have to stop being failing, or `TOTAL 0` would have
  to be reached by narrowing what is scanned (`DEFAULT_ROOTS`,
  `SCANNED_EXTENSIONS`, the allowlist filter) or by adding a token to the
  allowlist: **stop**, name the file and the line, and do not quiet the row
  (HS-7). `REPORT_ONLY` stays `false` and stays the only line this card changes
  in that file.
- A `tsc` error or a red assertion in a file this card does not own: a
  `BLOCKED` return with the compiler output. Do not make a field optional to
  quiet the compiler and do not relax an assertion (HS-7).
- A key this card adds has no real es-MX string, or a date would have to reach
  a catalogue pre-formatted (`PrepView.tsx:174` and `BackupCard.tsx:393` are
  the known cases): **report** it with its key and its location rather than
  shipping the English or the `Aug 8, 2026`. A copy question is not a card
  defect — S2.7 and S2.8 own the copy — but an English string in `es-MX.ts` is
  neither copy nor catalogue.

# Contract excerpts (authoritative)

## C-LANG@1 Language, documents and jobs

**Built by** S2.1. **Proven by** S2.6, S4b.1, S5.6. **Consumers:** web,
server routes, AI prompts, guards, speech, spell check, formats, backup.

1. Setting `language` ∈ `en` | `es-MX`, default `en`. The server exposes
   `spanishAvailable: boolean`: true only when `APUNTA_DEV_SPANISH=1` (D12).
   When false, the Language control is hidden and `es-MX` is rejected by
   `PUT /api/settings` with code `language_unavailable`.
2. Locale mapping (one table in `shared/src/i18n/locales.ts`):

   | App | UI and `Intl` | Whisper `-l` | Speech model | Dictionary | Prompts |
   | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
   | `en` | unchanged from today | `en` | `ggml-tiny.en.bin` | current English | current |
   | `es-MX` | `es-MX` | `es` | per C-STT selection | per S1.5 | Spanish set |

3. Documents: migration adds `locale TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'en'` to notes
   and to formats. **All existing rows are `en`.** New notes take the job's
   locale. Existing notes and formats are never translated or relabelled.
4. Jobs capture `{ locale, sttModel, llmModel, promptSet }` at start
   (recording, transcription, draft, refine, plan, briefing, brainstorm).
   Retries, SSE and persistence use the captured context, never the current
   setting. **Refine uses the target note's locale**, whatever the UI
   language and whatever language the request is typed in.
5. Section roles: `shared/src/section-roles.ts` maps known section names in
   both languages (case- and accent-insensitive) to role IDs (`location`,
   `presentation`, `risk`, `discussion`, `intervention`, `actions`,
   `next_session`, and the SOAP and intake roles). Guards use roles, not
   strings. Unknown sections get role `custom`. Stored strings are not
   rewritten.
6. Changing Language is blocked while any job or save is active: the web
   control is disabled with a reason; the server also returns 409
   `language_change_blocked` if it knows of an active job.
7. Spanish dictation requires the Spanish speech model to be ready (C-ACQ).
   If it is not, dictation shows "Spanish speech model not installed" with
   a download action. **Spanish audio is never sent to the English model.**
8. The Spanish standard format is created as a separate format with
   `locale: 'es-MX'`; English formats are untouched. Imported formats take
   the UI language at import time; the user can change a format's locale.
9. Backups and restores carry the `locale` columns.

**Rejection example.** UI switched to Español, user refines an existing
English note with a Spanish instruction → the note stays English, the reply
explains the change in the note's language.

# Run configuration (v2 plan)

## 1. Ports

| Use | Port |
| --- | --- |
| Live instance: **never contact** | 7717 |
| Sandbox servers (C-ISO) | 7800 to 7889 |
| Updater test server (C-UPD) | 7890 to 7899 |
| Playwright under the sandbox | the port `sandbox.mjs env` assigns |

## 2. Gate levels

A card names one level. Commands run from the repository root unless a card
says otherwise. Until P0.3 is APPROVED, only L0 and the non-launching part of
L1 may run.

| Level | When | Commands |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **L0** docs only | cards that change only Markdown | `npx prettier --check <changed files>`; `node scripts/check-no-external-urls.mjs` |
| **L1** targeted | every implementation card | `npm run lint`; `npm run typecheck`; `npm run build:shared`, then the card's named test files with `npx vitest run <paths>` from the repository root (the root `vitest.config.ts` defines the projects) |
| **L2** parent acceptance | every parent review card | everything in §3 |
| **L3** native or real model | cards and parent reviews that say so | the card's listed commands, all through `sandbox.mjs` |

## 3. The L2 suite

```sh
npm run lint
npm run typecheck
TZ=UTC npm test
TZ=America/Denver npm test
TZ=America/Mexico_City npm test
TZ=Australia/Sydney npm test
npm run build
node scripts/v2/sandbox.mjs env --port 7810 > /tmp/apunta-v2-e2e.env && . /tmp/apunta-v2-e2e.env && npm run e2e
npm run eval -- --fake --runs 1
```

After P0.2, each `TZ=` run prints its effective zone (a test asserts it), so
four runs really exercise four zones. After P0.3, the e2e line is the only
permitted way to run Playwright. After S3.2, add
`npm run eval -- --fake --runs 1 --corpus e2e/fixtures/eval-es/tuning`.
After P3.3, add `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` and
`cargo test` in `src-tauri/`.

## 4. Evidence

- Write detailed output to `docs/v2/evidence/<card-id>/`. Keep it sanitized:
  replace sandbox paths with `<sandbox>`, the home folder with `~`, and never
  include hostnames, usernames, keys, tokens or real names.
- Raw logs stay in the sandbox run folder and are never committed.
- Each command's evidence records: working directory, exact command, exit
  code, start and end time, and a short excerpt (failures in full, up to 200
  lines).
- Status words: criteria `NOT RUN`, `PASS`, `FAIL`, `BLOCKED`; cards
  `NOT STARTED`, `IN PROGRESS`, `SUBMITTED`, `APPROVED`,
  `CHANGES REQUESTED`, `BLOCKED`; instruction reviews `CLEAR`, `DEFECT`,
  `UNKNOWN`. Every blank template starts at `NOT RUN` or `UNKNOWN`.

## Verdict

**FAIL** — two rows are red at the head commit under review, both from the same
cause: finding 1 (the uncommitted allowlist makes the bare check `TOTAL 2`, so
V1 exits 1 and `npm run lint` exits 1). Finding 2 is a second, independent
blocker: three call sites where the English on the screen changed, against Fixed
decision 7. Findings 1 and 2 are both small and neither needs May edit widened,
a guard loosened or an allowlist token invented. V2, V3 and V5 pass as written.
Nothing here is `BLOCKED`: every row ran on this box under Node 24.19.0, and no
stop condition in the card was hit.
